messages:
amanda: quick heads-up — replay run against prod-traces shows weird p99 tail when batch_width=8.

josh: can you paste the run config? was kv_cache enabled?

amanda: yes: `--batch-width 8 --kv-cache on --microbatch 2` and we used replay-tool v0.9. logs below.

amanda: ```
$ ./replay-tool --trace s3://traces/prod/2026-03-14.ndjson \\n    --batch-width 8 --microbatch 2 --kv-cache on \\n    --duration 30m \

# summary (tokens/sec, latency-ms)
# p50,p95,p99
2.4k, 22, 140
2.4k, 21, 145
2.4k, 20, 420  <-- spike window
```

li: hmm p99 jumps coincide with page faults? or kernel scheduling? did we pin threads?

rachel: we didn't in that run. Also kernel selection flipped to AVX path on those hosts in last deploy (kernel-level optimized BLAS).

emma: synthetic load doesn't show this, so it's likely cache-warmth + convoying: replay preserves inter-request prefixes and burstiness.

josh: propose three experiments: 1) pinned-thread replay with same trace, 2) synthetic constant-QPS but randomized prefixes, 3) trace-shuffled replay to break prefix locality.

amanda: agreed. also let's capture eBPF stack samples during p99 windows: `sudo ./trace-latency -p $(pidof redwood-runtime) -o /tmp/trace.pb`

dev-bot: perf job queued: `perf/job/1812345678-replay-pinned` scheduled at 2026-03-17T15:05Z by amanda

li: another note — our microbatch flush path acquires a global spinlock when microbatch size < shard_threshold, causing convoys under certain arrival patterns.

rachel: can we change to per-shard batched-queue (lock per shard)? tradeoff: more memory and bookkeeping but reduces global contention.

emma: if p99 is dominated by spinlock waits, then optimizing for p95 will be misleading — p95 can look great while tail suffers.

josh: exactly. synthetic load (smooth Poisson arrivals) hides convoys; replay (bursty arrivals, prefix locality) amplifies spinlock + KV-miss cascades. Measurement choice changes root cause.

amanda: action items: 
- amanda: run pinned replay + eBPF capture (today)
- josh: run synth with jittered arrivals and multiple seeds (today)
- li: prototype shard-queue and bench microbench (48h)
- rachel: check canary hosts and rollback AVX kernel path if we reproduce there (coord with infra)
- emma: produce p95/p99 histograms + cumulative tail plots and annotate with eBPF stacks (tomorrow)

josh: thanks — quick sync tomorrow 9am PT? :thumbsup:

amanda: SGTM. meet in #eng-runtime.
